prize_parts.citation: For the development of pH-sensitive ionizable lipid nanoparticles that encapsulate nucleic acids and release them inside cells, making nucleic-acid medicines deliverable.

statement.case_for: After round 1 I move from B008 to B009, with the Vancouver strand of Cullis, Hope and Madden. The reason is mostly maturity. The core is a physical-chemical design principle that I can assess from my own field: a lipid whose headgroup charge depends on pH lets one self-assembled particle load nucleic acid at low pH, stay near neutral in circulation, and become fusogenic in the acidic endosome, so the phase behaviour of the lipid is the delivery mechanism. The principle has been reproduced by many independent groups, and it carried both siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines to approved use. No other leading candidate combines a clear molecular principle with consequences already demonstrated at scale. Choosing the Vancouver trio answers my own round-1 worry about credit: it follows the earliest encapsulation and pH-dependent assembly work rather than a later optimisation strand. The 2023 Medicine prize rewarded the cargo modification, not the vehicle, so this does not repeat that prize.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point. Anderson and Langer's lipidoid libraries and in vivo delivery work, and MacLachlan's ionizable-lipid optimisation, fall outside a three-name cut, and the patent history makes priority arguments uncomfortable. A critic can say that the part which reached patients was iterative lipid and formulation optimisation, not a single discovery, and that the work sits closer to pharmaceutical technology and Medicine than to chemistry. I also work on lipid self-assembly, so I may be inclined to see a design principle where a synthetic or biological colleague sees engineering.

responses.point: Chabes argued that for condensates the open question is the mechanism itself, namely whether in vivo structures are equilibrium liquid-liquid phase separation at all, whereas for degraders the mechanism is measured and the open question is clinical efficacy.
responses.response: I accept this and it is the main reason I have moved off B008. In vitro, demixing of multivalent proteins is solid physical chemistry. The step to a defined cellular structure with a function is where the evidence is still contested, and I should not ask the committee to cite a principle whose cellular scope is unsettled. I do not agree that attribution is a decisive objection to B009, though. The Vancouver encapsulation and ionizable-lipid work is a coherent and datable strand. I disagree with you that B045 is therefore the safer choice, because it also needs a split between PROTAC and glue strands and leaves out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim, so its attribution problem is no smaller than that of B009.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B009 for Cullis, Anderson and Langer, with Cullis as the indispensable core and Anderson and Langer representing the lipid-library and in vivo delivery strand.
responses.response: I now agree with your first choice in substance but not in the trio. The pH-dependent ionizable lipid is the molecular idea, and it was established in the Vancouver work on encapsulation and fusogenic lipids before the lipidoid libraries. Anderson and Langer's contribution, the combinatorial route to potent lipids and in vivo siRNA delivery, is real, but it optimised and extended the principle rather than founding it. I would therefore keep Hope and Madden beside Cullis. I accept that this is a judgement and that you can fairly argue the other cut. If the committee prefers your trio, I would support it over any configuration I rank lower.

responses.point: Somfai holds that Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B069) has the cleanest attribution and the longest confirmation record, and that Zou's mechanistic argument separates it from the 2010 prize.
responses.response: I take the mechanistic point seriously. The move from tin amides to free amines with bulky phosphines and strong bases needed its own solution, so B069 is not just a scope expansion, and Buchwald and Hartwig is the least arbitrary pair on the list. My remaining difficulty is conceptual. It refines how a known bond is made, and it follows two recent synthetic-methodology prizes. I would rank it clearly above B008, and if the committee decides that attribution clarity should win over a design principle with contested credit, I could support it. I put it just behind my first choice. I did not make it an alternative only because I limited myself to the two that complement my own field.

responses.point: The chair asks whether any member would support a two-part prize and which pairing would be least arbitrary, given that the three-person limit forces a single laureate in the second part.
responses.response: I considered B009 with B008, or B009 with B045, and decided against both. Pairing forces me to cut the Vancouver trio to two names or to leave one part with a single name, and either cut would be arbitrary and weaker than a single well-defined part. I therefore propose one part. If the committee wants two parts, I would choose the pair that does not require a cut I cannot defend, and I would not pair B009 with B008 while the in vivo condensate question remains open.

uncertainties: Whether Hope and Madden or Anderson and Langer should stand with Cullis, and whether MacLachlan displaces any of them
Whether the committee regards ionizable lipid delivery as chemistry or as a medical technology belonging to Medicine
Whether a prize on mRNA delivery is seen as too close to the 2023 Medicine prize despite the vehicle and cargo being distinct
How much weight the committee gives to B045 maturity if a degrader is approved before the vote
statement.conflict_note: I work on lipid self-assembly and lipid-protein interaction, which overlaps scientifically with B009 and B008, and having moved to B009 I flag that my field is close to it. I have no personal, institutional or collaborative tie to Cullis, Hope, Madden or any other credited person that I know of. Aili's research overlap with mine on self-assembly is not at recusal level. My Lund colleagues Linke and Somfai have no stated link to these candidates. I do not think recusal is warranted, but the committee should discount my enthusiasm for B009 by my field closeness.
